model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The image presents a bar chart that illustrates the comparison of two different metrics, Per-Output and Per-Layer, against varying percentages of sparsity rates. The sparsity rates, ranging from 10% to 80%, are plotted along the horizontal axis, serving as the independent variable of the chart. The vertical axis represents the logarithmic scale of the output, indicated by the exponential notation at the top, which spans from left to right across the chart.

The Per-Output is denoted by blue bars and the Per-Layer by orange bars. Each bar's height corresponds to the respective metric's value at a given sparsity rate. The sparsity rates increase systematically from left to right, with numerical labels at each interval, such as 10%, 20%, 30%, and so forth, up to 80%.

The bars are organized in ascending order of sparsity rates, starting with 10% on the far left and ending with 80% at the far right. The values of the metrics appear to vary across the sparsity rates, with the Per-Output bars generally being shorter than the corresponding Per-Layer bars, indicating lower values for Per-Output at the same sparsity rate.

The chart lacks any additional visual cues such as grid lines, scale markers, or other annotations that could provide further insights into the data. The axes are not labeled with units or decimal separators, and there is no legend explaining the color coding of the bars beyond the direct labeling within the chart itself.
model_annotations.Chinese: This visual contains a series of two-color bar charts arranged in a diagonal flow chart, which collectively represent Mallorie E Bricker KG's data. Two primary variables are plotted against Sparsity Ratio, indicated by percentages on the x-axis and on the y-axis. The x-axis is categorical, with discrete percentage values increasing from left to right. The y-axis is on a logarithmic scale, labeled with Perplexity values ranging from 10^2 to 10^3, signaling a geometric progression. The bars extend upward and to the right, indicating that higher Sparsity Ratio correlates with higher Perplexity. In each set, Sparsity Ratio is represented on the x-axis, while the color Long Memory depicts the Perplexity. The uppermost blue and orange bars represent the Perplexity for the long memory and PART output, respectively, which are shorter compared to the ambient complexity. The heights of the bars increase from left to right, suggesting that longer memory and PART output generally lead to greater ambient complexity across different Sparsity Ratios.
model_annotations.German: Das Balkendiagramm stellt die Verteilung von Per-Output- und Per-Layer-Perplexitäten in Relation zu unterschiedlichen Sätzungsraten dar, wobei die Perplexität logarithmisch skaliert wird. Die horizontale Achse repräsentiert die Sätzungsrate, die von 10% bis 80% in festen Schritten aufsteigend angeordnet ist. Die vertikale Achse zeigt die Perplexität im logarithmischen Skalenbereich von 10^1 bis 10^3. Der Skalentyp der vertikalen Achse ist logarithmisch. Die Per-Output-Perplexitäten sind durch die Farbe orange dargestellt und die Per-Layer-Perplexitäten durch Blau. Der größte Wert für Per-Output-Perplexitäten tritt bei 80% Sätzungsrate auf, mit einer Perplexität nahe 1000. Per-Layer-Perplexitäten haben konstant niedrigere Werte im Vergleich zu Per-Output-Perplexitäten, wobei der höchste Wert bei 60% Sätzungsrate liegt und der niedrigste Wert bei 10% Sätzungsrate. Zu 80% Sätzungsrate werden die Per-Layer-Perplexitäten durch einen scharfen Anstieg in die Per-Output-Perplexität gegenübergestellt, wobei Per-Output-Perplexitäten einzigartig bei höherer Sätzungsrate und niedrigeren Perceptual-Höhen sind.
